abstract: At telecommunications wavelengths, free carriers generated by two-photon absorption limit optical parametric oscillation (OPO) in silicon. Here, we demonstrate telecom-band OPO in a passive silicon microring resonator without electrical carrier sweep-out, driven by a single continuous-wave (CW) pump at 4.5 K. We achieve an on-chip OPO onset power of 2.25 mW and a total conversion efficiency of 1.9% into all parametric sidebands at a pump power of 4.8 mW. Despite CW pumping, the parametric output emerges as a train of pulses synchronized with microsecond-scale self-pulsing. At higher pump powers, OPO emission is absent during intervals of sustained sub-GHz oscillations in the pump transmission, narrowing the temporal window for OPO. Furthermore, by adjusting the pump detuning, we observe OPO at temperatures up to 55 K. These results demonstrate that nonlinear cavity dynamics govern the temporal structure and operating conditions of cryogenic silicon OPOs, providing new insights into controlling the oscillation regimes and temporal characteristics of on-chip nonlinear light sources compatible with cryogenic quantum photonic circuits.
